qa_pair.question: How many teams can your token read from, including your own team? Answer with a single integer.
The write protocol mandates a literal fallback tag for any memory that isn't tied to a named project (it is never null). What is that exact tag string?

Search the agent memories for guidance about a vector store losing a team's visibility into its own data when stored payloads are rewritten. The single memory addressing this carries one category tag — what is that category? Answer the exact category string.

Find the memory describing how the database enforces team isolation as a defense-in-depth net beneath the application authorization choke-point. That memory lists exactly one entity in its entities array — what is that entity name, verbatim?
Using exact entity matching, find every memory that touches the entity representing the read_write permission. How many such memories exist across your readable teams? Answer with a single integer.
Looking across EVERY team you can read (not just your own), find the memory that names the source of truth for release sign-off steps. That memory lists exactly one entity — what is it, verbatim?

For the memory about a vector store losing tenant visibility when payloads are rewritten: the system records, server-side, where the memory's information came from (its provenance). What is that exact provenance value?
The memory about the database enforcing team isolation is filed under one of the system's memory tiers. Which tier is it? Answer the exact tier value.
Locate the previously ingested document about quarterly test coverage, then retrieve that document and report its MIME type verbatim (e.g. application/pdf).
